title: autotune: safer batching/caching defaults, new quantization profiles, and unit-econ tooling
author: Maya Patel
body:
Summary: This PR introduces an automatic tuning path for batching and KV-prefix caching defaults, adds a small set of vetted quantization profiles for common model families, and ships an initial unit-economics (UEcon) CLI and API that ties model serving parameters to cost-per-token estimates. Motivation: customers repeatedly ask for safer defaults that reduce cost regressions while not impacting tail latency or output quality. Manual tuning is error-prone and slows onboarding; the UEcon tooling and autotune defaults aim to give teams good out-of-the-box economics and a transparent knob for tradeoffs.

What changed (high level):
- runtime/autotune: add autotune controller that recommends batching.max_batch_size and prefix_cache.enabled based on observed request size distribution and SLO targets. Controller emits recommendations into the model config store and can optionally apply safe rollouts.
- runtime/config: new defaults feature flag redwood.autotune.defaults (off by default; enabled for new accounts in trial) and a documented safe-ramp plan.
- runtime/quant: add quant profiles (q4_0, q4_1, q8_0) with validated perf/cost/quality summaries for gpt-family and llama-style models; profiles live under /models/quant/profiles.yaml and are referenced by the model registry.
- tooling/uecon: add CLI `redwood uecon estimate` and server-side API endpoints to estimate per-route token cost given batching/caching/quant settings; exposes a clear delta vs baseline. Includes a small data schema for workload snapshots used by the estimator.
- console: surface recommended autosave options and unit-econ delta on the model settings page.
- docs: explain autotune lifecycle, safety checks, and how to run UEcon estimates.

Testing and validation:
- unit tests for autotune heuristics and quant profile parsers.
- integration tests exercising a synthetic workload (mixed short/long requests) verifying autotune recommendations reduce median cost-per-token vs naive defaults and do not increase 99.9th tail latency beyond configured SLO.
- perf canary run on a small dedicated pool for two days validating resource utilization and KV cache hit-rate improvements. Canary showed ~18% lower token cost for a sample e-commerce chat workload with no measurable tail-latency regression.

Rollout plan:
- Feature gated behind redwood.autotune.defaults. Default remains off for existing customers; enabled by opt-in.
- Gradual rollout via feature flags and canary pool for first 2-3 weeks.
- Monitor: per-route cost dashboard, tail latency SLOs, output-quality regression alerts (eval harness).

Related tickets: ENG-2198 (autotune controller), ENG-2210 (quant profiles validation), PM-412 (UEcon MVP).

Checklist: 
- [x] Unit tests added
- [x] Integration/canary validated
- [x] Docs updated
- [x] UX for console surfaced
- [x] Linear/Jira links included

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps the autotune controller conservative: it recommends changes but will only auto-apply if the customer has enabled safe-apply and the recommendation passes output-quality checks on a held-out prompt set. The quant profiles are intentionally small and documented with when-to-use guidance (quality-sensitive vs cost-sensitive workloads).
commits: c1a7d3e: runtime: add autotune controller and recommendation API
b8f3c52: runtime: introduce feature flag for autotune defaults and safe-ramp logic
9e4b1a0: quant: add q4_0/q4_1/q8_0 profiles and validation scripts
f2d6b77: tooling: add uecon CLI + server estimator; docs and console wiring
review_conversation: Diego Morales: How do we prevent noisy recommendations for very low-traffic routes?
Maya Patel: Controller uses a min-sample threshold (default 500 requests) before recommending; threshold is configurable per-customer.
Ava Chen: Can we add a toggle to disable auto-apply at the org level?
Maya Patel: Added org-level safe-apply flag and documented it in the console UX.
merge_summary: Merged by Ava Chen via squash merge. PR grouped related autotune defaults, quant profiles, and UEcon tooling into a single deployable. Changelog entry created under ops/RELEASE_NOTES.md.
release_notes: Introduce conservative autotune defaults for batching and caching, three validated quantization profiles (q4_0, q4_1, q8_0), and initial UEcon estimation tooling. Feature gated; opt-in for existing customers. Improves typical token-cost by ~15-20% on sample workloads without tail latency regressions.
notes_for_ops: Enable redwood.autotune.defaults via feature flag for selected canary orgs. Monitor dashboards: uecon-per-route, autotune-recommendations, kv-cache-hit-rate, tail-latency-99.9. If perf regressions observed, roll back feature flag and consult autotune/controller logs.
qa_steps: 1) Enable feature flag for a canary org. 2) Run sample workload traffic using tests/perf/canary_uecon_run.yaml. 3) Confirm recommendations appear in model settings and that the estimator reports lower per-token cost. 4) Verify that 99.9th latency stays within SLO. 5) Run eval harness to ensure no output-quality regressions.
